newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan refinery fire will cut jet fuel production.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan refinery fire will cut jet fuel production.

text.p: A fire and explosion on Thursday hit the northern Taoyuan refinery of Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp and would reduce its jet fuel production for up to a month, officials said.

The late-afternoon blaze struck one of the refinery's two hydro-desulfurisation units, which was closed for annual maintenance, and was extinguished within an hour, Chinese Petroleum president Wenent Pan told reporters.
One refinery worker suffered unspecified injuries that were not believed to be life-threatening, officials said.
Officials in the monopoly's Taipei office estimated the damaged unit's reopening would be delayed for up to a month, but declined to estimate the value of any lost production.
The routine maintenance started in early May and the fire struck on the same day the refinery unit was scheduled to be reopened, officials said.
Sources at the oil firm said the refinery now was likely to be run at less than half of its monthly capacity of 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel to allow for necessary repairs.
Some 200 firefighters and more than 30 pieces of firefighting equipment were mobilised to fight the fire.
The refinery, which mainly serves Taiwan's domestic market, is Chinese Petroleum's main production facility for jet fuel, supplying for the nearby Taipei international airport.
Investigators said they were trying to determine the cause of the initial fire, which triggered a series of hydrogen explosions in the hydro-desulfurisation unit, officials said.

The accident at Taoyuan was the second to hit Taiwan's oil giant on Thursday, coming just hours after a two-minute power outage in southern Kaohsiung that forced a costly shutdown of its huge No.5 naphtha cracker and a score of affiliated plants.
The cracker and affected plants would be brought back to normal operation by Saturday, officials said.

The Taoyuan fire was the latest in a series of accidents at the refinery in the past year that have aroused public concern over the state firm's management -- and forced the sacking of its president and chairman in late 1996.
